projectTitle: Robert Rauschenberg Foundation: Drupal 7 to Drupal 10
project_haiku: The Rauschenberg Foundation's site was Drupal 7, much of it trapped in Views, with the art records living in FileMaker. We moved it to Drupal 10 so editors can build pages, and the archive still imports.
project_footer_CTA: Inheriting a Drupal 7 site that only a developer can edit? The Rauschenberg Foundation was that project.
pageSummary:
The job

The Robert Rauschenberg Foundation stewards the artist's work, archive, programs, and residencies. By 2024 the public site was Drupal 7: dozens of content types, pages assembled entirely in Views, more than a thousand artwork records, and a FileMaker database as the source for much of the art and archive. Staff who were not developers could not safely change a page.

What we built

The site is Drupal 10. Simple pages were migrated by hand. Artworks, series, and archive records came across by script. Several near-duplicate "basic page" types collapsed into one. Editors compose the homepage and program pages in Layout Builder. Artwork and archive records import from FileMaker on a schedule through the Feeds FileMaker module: descriptive fields stay with FileMaker, and a few Drupal-only fields stay editable by curators. Search and filtering use Search API and Facets. On View and Public Collections became one map with two kinds of pins. Chronology was slated for an interactive timeline. Exhibition history moved from book pages to ordinary pages.

Outcomes

An editor can change a hero, a news block, or a program tile without editing a View. New artwork reaches the site from FileMaker without a retype. The public can search the art and see where work is on view.
